bandReport.notes:
Band ends the paper. p16 is the last page of the booklet (the source PDF has 17 pages, 0-16) and Q100 is the last printed item; its option (d) is the final printed content on the page, with nothing following it. No question runs past the end of the band.

Seam with b5 is clean: p14 (opened, NOT transcribed) carries Q91, Q92, Q93 and Q94, and all four are complete on that page - Q94's options run (a) to (d) at the foot of its column. Nothing straddles the p14/p15 boundary, so Q95 opens this band cleanly.

No Directions block and no 'Consider the following for the next N items' block occurs anywhere in this band, so no set is owned here and none is inherited from b5. Q100 does open with 'Consider the following statements with reference to the given figure', but that stimulus governs ONLY Q100 - the three numbered statements and the 'Which of the above statements are correct?' lead-out are all inside that single item. It is a statement-set question, not a multi-item Directions set, so it carries no context and no setLabel.

Mid-page column flow worth knowing for Q99: its stem sits at the foot of the LEFT column of p16 with no options beneath it, and its four options are printed at the TOP of the RIGHT column of the same page, above the '100.' label. This is ordinary two-column flow within one page, not a seam.

All six questions in this band carry a printed diagram (95, 96, 97, 98, 99, 100). No figure was described inside any stem.

questions.stem: Angles are shown in the given figure. What is value of \(\angle 1 + \angle 2 + \angle 3 + \angle 4 + \angle 5 + \angle 6 + \angle 7 + \angle 8\)?
questions.figureNote: p15, top of the LEFT column, between the '95.' label and the stem 'Angles are shown in the given figure'. A line diagram of four straight segments crossing one another to form four small triangles, two opening upward and two opening downward. Eight angles are marked with arcs and labelled with the bare numerals 1 to 8: 2 and 1 at upper left, 3 and 4 at upper right, 8 and 5 at left and right of the lower band, 7 and 6 at the bottom. Crop the whole diagram including every one of the eight numerals and every arc; the numerals sit close to the outer edge of the figure, so leave a margin on all four sides rather than tightening to the line work.
questions.flags: Printed stem reads 'What is value of' - the article 'the' is absent on the page. Transcribed as printed, not repaired.

questions.stem: In the given figure \(PQ\) is parallel to \(RS\), \(\angle AEF = 95^\circ\), \(\angle BHS = 110^\circ\), and \(\angle ABC = x^\circ\). Then what is the value of \(x\)?
questions.figureNote: p15, bottom of the LEFT column, below the '96.' label. Two vertical parallel lines drawn as double-headed arrows: PQ on the left (P at top, Q at bottom) and RS on the right (R at top, S at bottom). Two slanting transversals cross both verticals and meet at a point B on the right. Labels to include in the crop: P and R along the top edge; Q and S along the bottom edge; A and C at the two left-hand arrowheads; E, G, F and H at the four intersections; B at the right; and the three marked values 95 degrees (at A, upper left), 110 degrees (lower right, near H) and x (at B). The figure runs to the very foot of the page column - check the bottom labels Q and S are not clipped.

questions.stem: In the given figure \(AB\) is parallel to \(CD\) and \(AC\) is parallel to \(BD\). If \(\angle EAC = 40^\circ\), \(\angle FDG = 55^\circ\), \(\angle HAB = x^\circ\), then what is the value of \(x\)?
questions.figureNote: p15, RIGHT column, between the '97.' label and the stem 'In the given figure AB is parallel to CD'. Two horizontal double-headed lines: the upper one through A and B, the lower one through E, C, D and F. Two slanting transversals cut both horizontals, and a separate ray AH rises from A. Labels to include: H at the top; A and B on the upper line; E, C, D and F on the lower line; G at the lower arrowhead on the right; and the three marked values x (at A, right of the ray AH), 40 degrees (below A) and 55 degrees (at D). Include the arrowheads at the top and bottom of the slanting lines.

questions.stem: In the given figure, there are three semi circles \(ABC\), \(AEF\) and \(CDF\). The distance between \(A\) and \(C\) is 28 units and \(F\) is the mid-point of \(AC\). What is the total area of the three semi circles?
questions.figureNote: p16, top of the LEFT column, between the '98.' label and the stem. A large semicircle standing on the horizontal segment AC with B at its top, plus two smaller semicircles hanging below AC - one on AF with E at its lowest point, one on FC with D at its lowest point. Labels to include: B at the top; A at the left end of the horizontal segment, C at the right end, F at its midpoint on the segment itself; E and D below. Crop to include the E and D labels, which sit just under the two lower arcs.

questions.stem: What is the approximate area of the shaded region in the figure given?
questions.figureNote: p16, bottom of the LEFT column, below the '99.' label. A circle with an inscribed rectangle; the region inside the circle but outside the rectangle is hatched with diagonal lines. The four side labels printed on the rectangle must all be in the crop: 8 cm along the top side, 6 cm on the left side, 6 cm on the right side, 8 cm along the bottom side. The stem sits below the figure and gives no measurements at all, so a crop that loses any of the four labels makes the question unanswerable. The figure runs close to the foot of the column.
questions.flags: The booklet prints decimals with a RAISED MIDDLE DOT: the options read 15·3, 25·5, 28·4, 30·5 cm2 on the page (verified at 8x). Transcribed here with an ordinary full stop as the decimal separator, because a middle dot risks being read as a multiplication sign by the downstream blind derivation. Values are unambiguous and unchanged. Recording it because this is the pilot paper and the middle-dot convention is a project-wide decision that has not been settled for cds-maths - the sibling UPSC pipeline preserves U+00B7.

questions.stem:
Consider the following statements with reference to the given figure:

1. The sum of the areas of \(\triangle AOD\) and \(\triangle BOC\) is equal to the sum of the areas of \(\triangle AOB\) and \(\triangle DOC\).

2. \(\angle AOD = \angle BOC\)

3. \(AB + BC + CD + DA > AC + BD\)

Which of the above statements are correct?
questions.figureNote: p16, RIGHT column, between the '100.' label and the 'Consider the following statements' text. A quadrilateral with both diagonals drawn, meeting at an interior point marked O. Vertices are labelled A (upper left), B (upper right, sitting noticeably higher than A), C (lower right) and D (lower left); DC is horizontal along the bottom and AD is vertical on the left. Include all five labels A, B, C, D and O. Do not crop it down to a symmetric-looking box - the exact shape is what the three statements are tested against.
questions.flags: INVENTED SUBTOPIC. The catalog lists only 'Parallelograms', 'Trapezium, Rhombus and Kite' and 'Cyclic Quadrilaterals' under Quadrilaterals; the figure here is a general quadrilateral (not a parallelogram, and not stated to be a trapezium or cyclic), and the question is about the four triangles cut off by its diagonals plus a perimeter-versus-diagonals inequality. 'Quadrilaterals' is the correct chapter, so the chapter key is valid; the subtopic wording is mine and is offered to the catalog-extension pass.
